gpc-revenue.label: Research & Business Impact
gpc-revenue.text: Leading design for the digital transformation of a $8B e-commerce platform. Customer research uncovered a key insight: B2B parts lookup is fundamentally different from traditional e-commerce. Service advisors often have the part in hand; they need to identify it, not shop for it. The "ways of finding" strategy (keyword search, category search, part number lookup, job type, legacy PDF catalogs) delivered a 7% add-to-cart improvement representing a $32.8M lift in revenue for the pro segment (2025).

bolt.label: Bolt Design System
bolt.text: Design engineering team designed and built aglobal themeable design system end to end - Figma 1 to 1 with code. Adopted across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Reduced front-end development time by approximately 25%.

agentic.label: Agentic AI
agentic.text: In August 2022 (three months before ChatGPT launched), I developed a roadmap for the Future of NAPA AutoCare built around AI-assisted issue diagnosis (NATE: NAPA Automated Technology Expert), AR-guided repair walkthroughs, and agentic shop management. The CIO hired me to execute it.

merger.label: Truist · $66B Merger
merger.text: The SunTrust-BB&T merger created Truist, the largest banking merger since 2008. Inheriting an innovation studio with an uncertain future, I rebooted it by adding customer journey mapping and strategic foresight. This repositioning earned a partnership with Corporate Strategy to run a major foresight exercise using the Jobs to Be Done framework, ultimately presenting three future-of-banking scenarios to the CEO and C-suite.
merger.quote: Bill Rogers, the CEO of SunTrust, called the work "instrumental" in thinking that led to the merger.

truist-products.label: Truist Commercial Banking
truist-products.text: Rebuilt Commercial and Small Business banking products for the merged Truist entity. All product lines required unifying two distinct legacy systems under one coherent design language designed by my team.

delta.label: Delta Air Lines
delta.text: Created news.delta.com, the corporate communications platform that serves Delta's media relations, employee engagement, and storytelling. A unified editorial system for a global airline with 90,000 employees.

clients.label: Client Work
clients.text: As Practice Lead at Sparks Grove (North Highland's design & innovation agency) led the shift from traditional agency model to agile software development and lean product management. Earned National Impact Award (2016) for transforming agency positioning to Human Experience Design.

upwave.label: Upwave · Turner Broadcasting
upwave.text: Prescient IoT-driven digital health venture at the intersection of wearables and personalized content delivery. Partnered with IDEO for market validation and product-market fit. Introduced lean product methodology enabling daily release cycles. The product was ahead of mainstream wearable adoption: pre-Apple Watch.

emmy.label: Emmy Award · 2011
emmy.text: Primetime Creative Arts Emmy for Outstanding Creative Achievement in Interactive Media for the "Conan O'Brien Presents: Team Coco" app. Team project, I led the design and development of the automatic content recognition (ACR) technology that powered the live sync-to-TV interactive experience. This was a team award; my contribution was the underlying sync to tv platform.

patents.label: Granted Patents
patents.text: Two U.S. patents granted in 2015 for technology filed in 2011 at Turner Broadcasting. US9043821B2 covers automatic content recognition systems: the ability for a device to identify what's playing on a TV screen. US9167276B2 covers audience engagement technologies: systems for interactive second-screen experiences synchronized to live broadcast.

magicwall.label: CNN Magic Wall
magicwall.text: I brought the large-format multi-touch technology into CNN and brokered the relationship with the technology partner after seeing that the alternatives under consideration were not capable of the interaction model the network needed. My team designed and built the weather software shown here. CNN's election teams subsequently made the wall famous with their own election-night applications; that footage documents the wider adoption of the platform, not software built by my team.

ar.label: Mobile AR · 2005-2008
ar.text: Pioneered the first mobile augmented reality applications in the US in partnership with Georgia Tech, for NBA (billboard advertising interactions) and Cartoon Network (gaming). Using the Nokia N90, before the iPhone existed. At the time, AR was widely assumed to require dedicated hardware or desktop-class processing. By tracking mobile GPU power trajectories, I made the non-obvious bet that phones, not strapped on PCs, would be where AR first reached scale. That prediction proved correct.

fusionfall.label: Behavioral Design · FusionFall
fusionfall.text: Led behavioral design research for Cartoon Network's FusionFall with Immersyve and Richard Ryan, co-author of Self-Determination Theory and one of the world's most-cited psychologists. We translated motivation science into specific recommendations for onboarding, challenge, exploration, social play, and retention, giving the development team a behavioral framework for deciding what to change and why.

dissertation.label: March 1993
dissertation.text: Undergraduate dissertation "Colonizing Cyberspace" predicted the transformative potential of global networked information spaces: 3D visualization of internet communities, virtual worlds for business and leisure. Described concepts now called "spatial computing" (Apple Vision Pro, Meta Quest). Predicted virtual communities and their cultural impact.
dissertation.quote: Submitted March 1993. The Mosaic browser was publicly announced April 21, 1993.

backprop.label: Neural Networks · 1993
backprop.text: Pioneered early AI tooling by building back-propagation learning capabilities into Apple's HyperCard via custom commands, the same foundational algorithm powering today's LLMs.

bafta.label: Armchair Manager · BAFTA Nominee
bafta.text: Designed, produced, and technically architected Armchair Manager Football, including its database. Built for standard-definition interactive television (pre-HDTV), it let viewers assemble a squad of real footballers, predict match outcomes, and watch goals, bookings, substitutions, and results change their score in real time. In 2000, it became the first interactive television game ever nominated in BAFTA's Sports category.

two-way-games.label: Multiplayer Television · 2001
two-way-games.text: These networked games were delivered through standard-definition television (pre-HDTV), not through a conventional website or PC game. Viewers joined with a remote control and played through cable or satellite set-top boxes. Although the experience lived on television, Fruity4some's client was assembled from HTML and JavaScript modules, while the platform used Java services and broadcast-specific engines to manage live multiplayer sessions, scoring, chat, leaderboards, and unreliable back channels across multiple television platforms.

apple-award.label: Apple Design Award
apple-award.text: Winner of the Apple Design Project Award (Problem Analysis) in an international inter-university competition.
apple-award.brandMarkAlt: Apple Computer rainbow logo used from 1977 to 1998

rts-award.label: RTS Innovation Award
rts-award.text: Winner of the UK Royal Television Society (RTS) Innovation Award for CNN's World Cup Twitter Buzz, a realtime interactive data visualization experience

felix.label: Felix the Cat · Interactive Comic
felix.text: Designer and producer of Felix the Cat's Giant Electronic Comic Book — stories, songs, and activities for ages 4–8 on Philips CD-i and PC CD-ROM, built at Epic Multimedia Group.
